definition: Ritalin is a brand name for methylphenidate hydrochloride, a synthetic stimulant that acts on the central nervous system. It appears to increase activity in brain systems involved in arousal and alertness and, in some clinical situations, may improve cognitive function.

provenance.scope: Source record C646; pinned source text

reasons: The packet does not state that Ritalin is a brand name; it identifies the substance as methylphenidate hydrochloride.

The wording about increasing activity in brain systems involved in arousal and alertness is broader than the packet’s support, which refers specifically to activating the brain stem arousal system and cortex to produce a stimulant effect.

The definition states that “Ritalin is a brand name for methylphenidate hydrochloride,” but the packet only describes methylphenidate hydrochloride as a synthetic central nervous system stimulant and does not support the claim that Ritalin is its brand name.

The definition says it “appears to increase activity in … arousal and alertness,” but the packet specifically mentions activation of the “brain stem arousal system and cortex” and does not mention “alertness.”

While “may improve cognitive function” is supported, the rest of the surrounding phrasing (“increase activity… in… arousal and alertness” and the “brand name” framing) is not fully supported by the packet.
